skill.title: CLI parameter normalization utility
skill.trigger: Use when a CLI collects raw '-p/--params' option strings and a dedicated parser normalizes 'path:comma,separated' tokens into a canonical list of per-file parameter lists consumed by repository and command handlers.
knowledge: A parser component is responsible for transforming raw CLI param tokens into the canonical shape list[dict[path->list[str]]] and preserving token order within each path group.

The parser boundary owns default-file mapping for empty-path tokens (e.g. map '' to a default params file) and must guarantee callers receive one canonical representation regardless of how options were supplied.

Callsites (CLI collector, Repo.run, command handlers) must supply an iterable of raw token strings; the parser owns normalization and should be defensive about None, single-string, or nested shapes before producing the canonical structure.

skill.title: Distinguish caller input shape from parser tokenization failures
skill.trigger: Use when a param-normalization parser returns an empty or unexpected canonical collection despite non-empty CLI arguments and it's unclear whether tokens were discarded by the parser or never reached it in the expected shape.
knowledge: Compare recorded values at the parser boundary and inside its loop: the raw path_params argument, each path_param, the split into (path, params_str), and the params list after splitting/filtering.

Map observations to causes: (a) path_params is None/empty → caller/CLI collector likely at fault; (b) path_params contains expected strings but ret stays empty or missing keys → parser (early return, grouping, or defaulting bug); (c) tokens present but filtered to empty → tokenization/filtering logic in parser.

Rank the earliest boundary that changes collection membership or shape above components that only propagate it; if inspection is inconclusive, preserve both caller and parser as competing candidates until further runtime evidence resolves the divergence.

skill.title: Descriptor-based gated assignment that forwards writes to an instance-held callable
skill.trigger: Use when a descriptor mediates instance attribute writes by checking an instance-held gate flag and, when allowed, invoking a callable stored on the instance with the assigned value or a substituted value.
knowledge: A descriptor separates gating logic from the stored-callable responsibility: it checks instance gate state and then decides whether and how to invoke the instance-held target.
The descriptor boundary owns the contract to forward the assigned value unchanged unless an explicit substitution policy applies; callers expect their assigned value to reach the target callable.

Instances expose two distinct roles: a gate-state holder (e.g. _handle) that controls whether the descriptor invokes the target, and an instance-held target callable (e.g. _assignable) that performs the actual effect.

skill.title: Diagnose descriptor argument substitution versus target callable ignoring the argument
skill.trigger: Use when a descriptor mediates property-sets and an assigned non-None value appears to reach the stored callable as None.
knowledge: Capture the assigned value at the caller, the value observed immediately inside the descriptor before it decides/ invokes, and the value received by the stored callable (wrap or instrument the target) to compare across boundaries.

If the descriptor observes the original non-None but the stored callable receives None, implicate the stored callable or its wrapper; if the descriptor observes None while the caller provided non-None, implicate inverted conditional or explicit substitution in the descriptor.

Rank the earliest boundary that changes the argument value above later propagators; if all observations match the assigned value but behavior is still wrong, preserve competing candidates and collect additional context (callable identity, defaults, wrappers).

skill.title: Modular QR-code image renderer (QR model, ImageFactory, format renderers, color-masks)
skill.trigger: Use when a repository separates a QR model that builds a module matrix from pluggable ImageFactory implementations that hand that matrix to format-specific renderers (XML emitters or bitmap painters) and separate color-mask/style utilities.
knowledge: The QR model constructs a boolean/module matrix and does not perform format-specific rendering.
ImageFactory.make_image delegates to a renderer object that implements process/save and is responsible for serializing output to a file-like object or stream.
Format-specific renderers (SVG XML emitters vs bitmap painters) own the serialization contract: which runtime object they hand to stdlib serializers and which keyword arguments are valid.
Color-mask and style utilities own color-mapping responsibilities and must present a stable per-pixel contract (value shape, transparency flag) rather than depending on renderer internals.

skill.title: Diagnose stdlib serializer misuse: wrong callee object vs unsupported kwargs
skill.trigger: Use when a format-specific serializer raises an error from a stdlib write() call (e.g., TypeError about keyword args) and it's unclear whether the renderer passed the wrong object (Element vs ElementTree) or used kwargs the actual object doesn't accept.
knowledge: Capture the actual object passed to write at runtime and inspect its type and available write signature (e.g., Element vs ElementTree and which kwargs it accepts).

If the object is an Element and Element.write rejects the kwargs while ElementTree.write accepts them, implicate the renderer constructing/passing the wrong object and rank renderer.save/_write highest.

If the object is an ElementTree but write still errors for the provided kwargs, implicate the renderer for supplying unsupported keyword args (or a Python-implementation mismatch) and rank the code that sets those kwargs highest.

If no callsite is found, search for helpers/wrappers or monkeypatches that create or forward the element/tree; when observations are inconclusive, preserve both renderer and stdlib-writer candidates instead of picking a winner.

skill.title: Terminal progress-display library with separated controller, renderer, and output sink
skill.trigger: Use when a repository implements a progress display by separating a controller that advances logical progress and schedules updates, renderer(s) that assemble complete terminal frames from canonical state, and output sinks that emit frames to a terminal or stream.
knowledge: A controller component owns logical progress state and an advance/iteration boundary and is responsible for scheduling update ticks; it should not perform formatting or direct IO.
Renderer components accept canonical progress state and formatting helpers and produce complete frames (string/bytes) while guaranteeing ordering and completeness for each produced frame.
Output sinks (stream/writer abstractions) own terminal emission and serialization; they accept complete frames and must not drop or reorder frames produced by renderers.
A ticker/timer drives periodic controller updates and context/lifecycle managers own startup and shutdown that span these boundaries.

skill.title: Locate missing or mischecked-out sources and map hypothesized component roles
skill.trigger: Use when localization hypothesizes component roles (e.g., controller -> renderer -> sink) but repository inspection returns no source files or package metadata and the immediate question is whether expected files exist and which implement those roles.
knowledge: First verify repository health by searching for package entrypoints and metadata in order: package __init__/module files, pyproject.toml or setup.cfg, README, and common module dirs; persistent absence suggests mischeckout/packaging rather than a code bug.

If files are present, map hypothesized roles by lightweight heuristics: find iterator/advance-style methods for controllers, render/format methods that return frames for renderers, and write/emit methods for sinks; prefer matches with signatures and naming conventions before ranking them as culprits.

Only change component ranking after confirming file presence and a role-appropriate match; if no files are found, escalate toward repository/packaging/checkout issues instead of selecting a code-level offender.

skill.title: Mock cloud-service admin endpoint that enqueues per-service runtime result tuples
skill.trigger: Use when an admin HTTP endpoint accepts external JSON to configure canned per-service results by calling a central API-backend setter which enqueues tuples into per-service in-memory queues that later service runtimes consume to produce SDK responses and write objects to storage.
knowledge: An admin HTTP component accepts external configuration payloads and translates caller JSON into a canonical result tuple shape before delegating to the central API-backend setter.

The API-backend setter owns the enqueue contract: it must record per-service (and per-account/region) ordered tuples with a stable tuple shape (e.g., (is_failure, data)) and not transform or drop elements expected by consumers.

Service runtime handlers consume those per-service queues to decide response headers (output vs failure locations) and to persist the configured content to object storage; they rely on the queue contract for ordering and content shape.

skill.title: Repository site-scoped DataIndex manager with owner/caller lifecycle boundary
skill.trigger: Use when a Repo lazily opens and caches a site-scoped on-disk index DB and higher-level index/view code or operations obtain transient per-filesystem index objects that callers must close.
knowledge: The Repo component owns the persistent DataIndex lifecycle: it lazily opens, caches, commits, and closes the on-disk DB placed at a site-scoped location.

Index/IndexView builders and transfer operations (fetch/push, remote handlers) may borrow the persistent DataIndex or produce transient per-filesystem DataIndex/views that callers are responsible for closing.

The owner/caller boundary must provide a clear contract for absence: either the owner returns a sentinel/no-op index when DB is disabled or callers must treat a None return as absence and avoid invoking lifecycle methods on it.

skill.title: Distinguish owner-absent resource from collector-introduced None entries
skill.trigger: Use when a lazily-owned resource (property/getter) may be None and callers iterate over a collected iterable of resources and unconditionally call lifecycle methods, causing AttributeError when None appears in the collection.
knowledge: Snapshot the value at the owner boundary (call the getter or read the stored owner field) and then snapshot the collector output before callers perform lifecycle actions; compare presence/absence of the resource at each point.

If the owner snapshot is None while callers expected an object, implicate the owner/lifecycle contract; if the owner snapshot is a valid object but the collector iterable contains None elements, implicate the collector/adapter that inserts placeholders for missing per-target indexes.

Rank the earliest boundary that changes the resource presence (owner -> collector -> caller) above later propagators; if observations are identical, preserve both candidates and collect richer context (call stacks, config flags, and collector implementation) before changing rankings.

skill.title: Service backend with thin Response handlers and explicit response<->model serialization boundary
skill.trigger: Use when HTTP/SDK handlers parse API parameters and call backend model methods that store domain objects and metadata, and API responses are assembled by serializing those model objects back into JSON across multiple endpoints.
knowledge: Response handlers are responsible for parsing/normalizing request parameters and passing a canonical representation to backend model methods; the parser must not silently drop tokens expected by callers.
Backend/domain models own persisted runtime metadata (e.g., execution parameters, prepared-statement references) and must expose that state through a stable field contract on model objects.

The response<->model serialization boundary owns the contract to include model metadata in each API operation that semantics require; different endpoints may assemble responses from different model objects and must explicitly copy metadata when needed to avoid silent omission.

skill.title: Distinguish caller input shape from parser tokenization failures
skill.trigger: Use when a param-normalization parser returns an empty or unexpected canonical collection despite non-empty CLI arguments and it's unclear whether tokens were discarded by the parser or never reached it in the expected shape.
knowledge: Compare recorded values at the parser boundary and inside its loop: the raw path_params argument, each path_param, the split into (path, params_str), and the params list after splitting/filtering.

Map observations to causes: (a) path_params is None/empty → caller/CLI collector likely at fault; (b) path_params contains expected strings but ret stays empty or missing keys → parser (early return, grouping, or defaulting bug); (c) tokens present but filtered to empty → tokenization/filtering logic in parser.

Rank the earliest boundary that changes collection membership or shape above components that only propagate it; if inspection is inconclusive, preserve both caller and parser as competing candidates until further runtime evidence resolves the divergence.

skill.title: Distinguish caller input shape from parser tokenization or later-serialization omission
skill.trigger: Use when request-derived parameter collections appear non-empty at some boundaries but an API response or endpoint returns an empty or missing canonical collection and it's unclear whether tokens were discarded by parsing/normalization or lost later during model-to-response assembly.
knowledge: Record/compare the parameter value at three boundaries: the raw extractor output (parser boundary), the canonical value passed into backend/model methods, and the fields present on the stored model instance used to build each response.

Map observations to causes: (a) raw extractor empty or None → caller/collector likely at fault; (b) raw extractor non-empty but canonical value passed to backend empty → parser normalization/tokenization bug (filtering, early return, grouping); (c) parser and model storage contain the parameters but a particular API response omits them → serialization/response-assembly omission.

Rank the earliest boundary that demonstrably changes collection membership or shape above components that only propagate values; if comparisons are inconclusive, preserve competing candidates (caller, parser, serializer) until further runtime evidence resolves the divergence.

skill.title: Terminal text cell sanitizer with width detector and marker inserter
skill.trigger: Use when a repository converts raw text into a sanitized stream of terminal cells by stripping ANSI escapes, iterating graphemes, classifying each grapheme as narrow or wide, inserting spacing/marker tokens tied to those graphemes, and formatting into output cells.
knowledge: Sanitizers separate responsibilities: ANSI/escape removal, grapheme iteration, width classification, per-grapheme marker/spacer insertion, and final cell formatting; each stage hands a canonical representation to the next.
The width-detector boundary is the single source of truth for grapheme width (narrow/wide) and must present a stable classification contract used by inserters and formatters.

The marker-inserter must deterministically apply the detector's classification to the same grapheme (preserving order and indices); inverted predicates or off-by-one insertions indicate a contract mismatch between detector and inserter.

The cell-builder consumes sanitized tokens and is responsible for preserving column-width accounting (including across ANSI sequences) but must not alter which graphemes were classified or marked by earlier stages.

skill.title: Filesystem-backed artifact Output manager
skill.trigger: Use when a repository models artifacts with an Output/object that owns canonical metadata, resolves a storage filesystem and canonical path, and derives hash information from a metadata model and per-file entries.
knowledge: An Output-like component owns a canonical metadata model (Meta/HashInfo) and a derived hash contract that callers use to make filesystem and cache decisions.

The initialization boundary converts serialized/cloud-encoded fields into a plain dict, then constructs Meta/HashInfo objects from that dict before performing filesystem resolution or version coalescing.

Filesystem/backend resolution and canonical path derivation occur after metadata conversion and may update version identifiers; hash-name and hash-info computation must derive from the canonical Meta/HashInfo and any merged per-file metas.

skill.title: Diagnose undefined local variable in constructor vs upstream missing input
skill.trigger: Use when a NameError for a local name occurs during object construction and it's unclear whether the constructor failed to bind the name on all control paths or callers/helpers left no data to assign.
knowledge: Check the constructor source for an unconditional assignment to the suspect name on every control path before any use; absence implies a local scoping/typo bug and ranks the constructor highest.

If the constructor binds the name but only conditionally, inspect all call sites and helpers for cases where inputs are omitted or a translator returns an empty/None shape that prevents the assignment; such evidence ranks callers/helpers higher.

Reproduce the call with minimal canonical inputs: invoke the constructor with the simple default/empty payload used by callers; if the NameError reproduces without external helpers, prefer fixing the constructor; if only reproduced via specific callers, prefer callers/helpers.

skill.title: Service backend with thin Response handlers and explicit response<->model serialization boundary
skill.trigger: Use when HTTP/SDK handlers parse API parameters and call backend model methods that store domain objects and metadata, and API responses are assembled by serializing those model objects back into JSON across multiple endpoints.
knowledge: Response handlers are responsible for parsing/normalizing request parameters and passing a canonical representation to backend model methods; the parser must not silently drop tokens expected by callers.
Backend/domain models own persisted runtime metadata (e.g., execution parameters, prepared-statement references) and must expose that state through a stable field contract on model objects.

The response<->model serialization boundary owns the contract to include model metadata in each API operation that semantics require; different endpoints may assemble responses from different model objects and must explicitly copy metadata when needed to avoid silent omission.

skill.title: Service backend with explicit response<->model serialization boundary and interchangeable backends
skill.trigger: Use when API/SDK response builders assemble JSON by serializing backend model objects and the repository contains multiple backend implementations (e.g., a simple in-memory model and a parser/executor) plus centralized encoding utilities.
knowledge: Backend model objects own canonical runtime fields (e.g., execution_input) and must document whether each field holds a native runtime type or a pre-serialized string; callers and response builders must not assume a single implicit representation.

When multiple backend implementations exist, each backend must honor the same field-representation contract or provide a conversion adapter at the backend/response boundary so response assembly sees a single canonical shape.

The response<->model serialization boundary is responsible for final JSON/datetime encoding or for explicitly forwarding pre-serialized values; implementing both (model pre-serialization plus response-layer serialization) causes double-encoding and must be avoided.

skill.title: Asyncio-style timeout context manager with scheduled handler and recorded task
skill.trigger: Use when a context manager schedules a loop callback to cancel the current coroutine and stores both a scheduled handler and a reference to the running Task while enter/exit code manages scheduling, exception conversion, and cleanup.
knowledge: The context manager separates scheduling (creating a loop callback handle) from ownership of the running Task: it records the current Task and the scheduled handler as two coordination references.

The scheduled handler is responsible for invoking cancel() on the recorded Task and performing the state transition that marks a timeout; after doing so it must release its references to avoid leaving stale pointers.

Enter/exit and cleanup code must schedule or cancel the handler, convert CancelledError into a TimeoutError when the state indicates an enforced timeout, and clear the recorded Task reference on exit to preserve state-machine invariants and avoid races between handler and synchronous cleanup.

skill.title: Parse-tree PEP8 normalizer with explicit indentation-node stack
skill.trigger: Use when a parse-tree normalizer visits token/leaf parts and maintains an explicit indentation-node stack of node objects whose .type values are defined by a small enum-like set of indentation constants.
knowledge: The normalizer boundary owns creation, mutation, and lifetime of indentation nodes (Bracket/Backslash/Implicit) and exposes a top-of-stack contract used by validators and node constructors.
A compact set of indentation-type constants is the stable cross-component contract: node constructors, normalizer rules, and any incremental/diff parser must agree on those names and membership.
Push/pop invariants matter: a push must create a node with a documented .type and a matching pop must restore the previous top; comparisons to .type assume the constant set is complete and stable.

skill.title: Locate missing symbol origin: internal removal/rename vs external or stale caller
skill.trigger: Use when runtime AttributeError names a missing enum/constant member but repository source and greps contain no references to that member.
knowledge: Compare symbol presence across locations: (1) source tree, (2) built artifacts (build/lib), and (3) external/runtime callers (stack traces, installed packages); presence inside source implicates internal rename, presence only in build/lib implicates packaging/build divergence.

Search for textual references and attribute access patterns (IndentationTypes.COMMA, getattr/[] usages) and inspect runtime stack traces to map the access to an in-repo or out-of-repo module; internal references rank definition or caller fixes higher.

Only change ranking when evidence selects one alternative: if repo sources reference the name, rank internal caller/definition edits; if only external artifacts or installed packages reference it, rank packaging/stale builds or external callers; if inconclusive, preserve both hypotheses and gather a runtime trace.

skill.title: Configuration-driven parameter dependency subsystem (ParamReader + snapshot + dependency object)
skill.trigger: Use when a repository loads parameter files via format-specific parsers, stores per-dependency snapshots for locks/CLI, and exposes dependency objects that merge snapshots and compare live file values to produce per-parameter status.
knowledge: Format-specific loaders (ParamReader role) parse files and extract requested key-path mappings; they produce a canonical mapping or an empty mapping for a present but empty file and must not silently drop keys with falsy values.

A per-dependency snapshot container (HashInfo-like role) holds the canonical mapping used in locks or CLI snapshots; dependency objects provide a fill_values boundary that merges such mappings into the dependency snapshot rather than treating falsy values as absent.

The dependency object owns file-existence validation and the workspace-status comparison contract: it must signal a missing parameters file distinctly (absence/None) while preserving keys whose values are falsy so per-key membership and value comparisons are meaningful.

skill.title: Plugin-style service-backend registry with dynamic module importer and per-account/region BackendDicts
skill.trigger: Use when a central dispatcher normalizes public service identifiers, consults alias/mapping tables, dynamically imports a resolved module, and returns a module-level BackendDict that provides per-account and per-region backend instances.
knowledge: A dispatcher normalizes incoming service names, applies alternate-name mappings, and uses a dynamic importer to load the resolved module's module-level BackendDict which is the canonical entry point for that service.

The module-level BackendDict and its AccountSpecificBackend lazily create per-region BaseBackend instances on first access; region lists are produced by a cached session/region generator and a concurrency lock coordinates creation/reset.

Name normalization often involves separate maps (module remap vs backend-attribute remap); the importer must derive the backend-attribute name from the final resolved module key (not the original raw name) to avoid mismatched getattr lookups.

skill.title: VCS-backed repository manager with FileSystem root-discovery and SCM fallback
skill.trigger: Use when a Repo-like initializer delegates parent-directory traversal to a FileSystem abstraction to locate a repository marker and an orchestration step applies SCM fallbacks and computes site-scoped paths for instance initialization.
knowledge: A Repo initializer separates a root-discovery role that walks parent directories via an abstract FileSystem from an orchestration/initialization role that consumes discovery results and sets canonical instance paths (e.g., root_dir, repo_dir, site-cache paths).

The root-discovery component relies on FileSystem primitives (abspath, isdir, join) and exposes a contract: return a canonical absolute root_dir or raise a documented NotARepo/NotFound error so callers can deterministically derive site-scoped locations.

The orchestration/initialization boundary applies SCM fallbacks, derives site-scoped cache/config paths, and must treat discovery as an explicit input (handle errors and returned values) rather than relying on discovery internals or implicit local bindings.

skill.title: Grammar-driven concrete-syntax-tree parser with Normalizer/ErrorFinder validators
skill.trigger: Use when a parser produces a concrete syntax tree of Node/Leaf objects and a Normalizer/ErrorFinder walks the tree applying per-node SyntaxRule validators that inspect ancestor chains and helper utilities (paren-skipping, paren-removal) to decide context-sensitive syntax issues.
knowledge: The parser boundary produces concrete node.type roles (container vs atom vs leaf); Normalizer rules must rely on these stable parent-role contracts rather than incidental traversal artifacts.

Ancestor-selection helpers (e.g., skip-parens or remove-parens) and the choice to use node.parent are part of the Normalizer-to-parser boundary contract and must be consistent with parser-produced CST shape for all supported versions.

Validators enforcing positional or count constraints (assignment-list/starred-element rules, comp-for contexts) should operate on canonical container roles and guard when indexing children to avoid misclassifying nodes wrapped in parentheses or atoms.

skill.title: Distinguish caller input shape from parser tokenization or later-serialization omission
skill.trigger: Use when request-derived parameter collections appear non-empty at some boundaries but an API response or endpoint returns an empty or missing canonical collection and it's unclear whether tokens were discarded by parsing/normalization or lost later during model-to-response assembly.
knowledge: Record/compare the parameter value at three boundaries: the raw extractor output (parser boundary), the canonical value passed into backend/model methods, and the fields present on the stored model instance used to build each response.

Map observations to causes: (a) raw extractor empty or None → caller/collector likely at fault; (b) raw extractor non-empty but canonical value passed to backend empty → parser normalization/tokenization bug (filtering, early return, grouping); (c) parser and model storage contain the parameters but a particular API response omits them → serialization/response-assembly omission.

Rank the earliest boundary that demonstrably changes collection membership or shape above components that only propagate values; if comparisons are inconclusive, preserve competing candidates (caller, parser, serializer) until further runtime evidence resolves the divergence.

skill.title: Compare CST parent chain versus Normalizer ancestor-selection
skill.trigger: Use when a CST-based validator flags a context-sensitive syntax node (e.g., starred expression) and it's unclear whether the parser produced an unexpected parent chain or the Normalizer's ancestor-selection helpers or parent-rule logic misidentify the surrounding role.
knowledge: Record the node's immediate parent chain from the parser output (sequence of node.type values up to the nearest meaningful container) and separately record the ancestor the Normalizer helper returns for the same node and runtime version.

If the parser chain contains a container role but the Normalizer helper returns a different role (atom or direct child), implicate the Normalizer's ancestor-selection helper or its use of node.parent; rank fixes to ancestor selection highest.

If the ancestor matches the expected container role but validators still reject the node, implicate the parent-rule validation (positional/count checks) and rank changes to those checks above code that only reports or propagates issues; if comparisons are inconclusive, preserve both parser and Normalizer candidates until further runtime evidence resolves the divergence.
